rule.body: Choose "a" or "an" by the first SOUND, not the first letter: an hour, a university, an MBA. Use "the" for unique things, superlatives, rivers and oceans, and groups such as "the rich". Use no article with meals and with "go to school/church" when you go for the usual purpose. "A few" and "a little" mean some; "few" and "little" mean hardly any. Use few/many/fewer with countable nouns and little/much/less with uncountable ones.
rule.example: An honest man had a little time, so he went to the school to see the principal.

questions.stem: In a fair society, ___ pay more tax than the poor.
questions.explanation: "The" + adjective names a whole group of people: the rich, the poor. "Riches" means wealth, not people.

questions.stem: Amaka hopes to win a scholarship to ___ European university.
questions.explanation: "European" begins with a "yoo" sound, which is a consonant sound, so we use "a", not "an".

questions.stem: ___ Niger is one of the longest rivers in Africa.
questions.explanation: Names of rivers take "the": the Niger, the Benue, the Nile.

options.A: We have breakfast at seven every morning.
options.B: We have the breakfast at seven every morning.
options.C: We have a breakfast at seven every morning.
options.D: We have an breakfast at seven every morning.

questions.explanation: Names of meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) normally take no article when we talk about daily routine.

questions.stem: I still have ___ friends in Kano, so I will not feel lonely when I visit.
questions.explanation: "A few" means some, which fits "will not feel lonely". "Friends" is countable, so "little" and "a little" are wrong.

questions.stem: Kunle is so rude that he has ___ friends, if any.
questions.explanation: "Few" without "a" means hardly any, which matches "if any". "Friends" is countable, so not "little".

questions.stem: Don't worry; we still have ___ time, so let us eat before we leave.
questions.explanation: "Time" is uncountable, and "a little" means some, which fits "don't worry". "Little" alone would mean hardly any.

questions.stem: There are ___ cars on this road today than there were yesterday.
questions.explanation: "Cars" is a countable plural noun, so standard English uses "fewer". "Less" goes with uncountable nouns.

questions.stem: Which of the following is correctly written?
questions.explanation: "MBA" is said "em-bee-ay", a vowel sound, so "an". The others should be "an hour-long", "a one-day" and "a useful".

questions.stem: Mr Okafor, a parent, ___ to discuss his son's poor results with the principal.
questions.explanation: "Go to school" means going as a student. A parent visiting the building goes to "the school".
